text: A proportional controller changes its output in proportion to the current difference between the target and the measured value.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: John D. Hedengren, APMonitor Process Dynamics and Control, proportional-control lesson; https://apmonitor.com/pdc/index.php/Main/ProportionalControl. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: A proportional controller may need a persistent error to maintain the output required by a steady load. More gain can reduce this offset but changes the system's response.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: John D. Hedengren, APMonitor Process Dynamics and Control, proportional-control lesson; https://apmonitor.com/pdc/index.php/Main/ProportionalControl. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: Integral action accumulates error over time. It can keep changing the control output even when the instantaneous error is small.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: John D. Hedengren, APMonitor Process Dynamics and Control, PI lesson; https://apmonitor.com/pdc/index.php/Main/ProportionalIntegralControl. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: A PI controller combines a response to present error with a response to accumulated error, often removing the offset left by proportional control.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: John D. Hedengren, APMonitor Process Dynamics and Control, PI lesson; https://apmonitor.com/pdc/index.php/Main/ProportionalIntegralControl. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: When switching from manual operation to automatic control, matching the controller's initial output to the current output can avoid an abrupt jump.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: John D. Hedengren, APMonitor Process Dynamics and Control, PI lesson; https://apmonitor.com/pdc/index.php/Main/ProportionalIntegralControl. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: Derivative action responds to how quickly a measured process variable is changing. It can damp oscillation but also magnify measurement noise.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: John D. Hedengren, APMonitor Process Dynamics and Control, PID lesson; https://apmonitor.com/pdc/index.php/Main/ProportionalIntegralDerivative. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: Filtering a derivative estimate reduces its sensitivity to rapid measurement noise, at the cost of adding lag.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: John D. Hedengren, APMonitor Process Dynamics and Control, PID lesson; https://apmonitor.com/pdc/index.php/Main/ProportionalIntegralDerivative. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: A sudden target change can create a large derivative response if the controller differentiates error. Differentiating the measured variable instead avoids this target-induced kick.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: John D. Hedengren, APMonitor Process Dynamics and Control, PID lesson; https://apmonitor.com/pdc/index.php/Main/ProportionalIntegralDerivative. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: When an actuator stays at its limit, accumulated integral error can keep the controller saturated after conditions change. Anti-windup methods limit this accumulation.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: John D. Hedengren, APMonitor Process Dynamics and Control, PID lesson; https://apmonitor.com/pdc/index.php/Main/ProportionalIntegralDerivative. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: A digital PID controller replaces a continuous integral with a sum and estimates rate of change from successive samples. The sample interval is part of the calculation.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: John D. Hedengren, APMonitor Process Dynamics and Control, PID lesson; https://apmonitor.com/pdc/index.php/Main/ProportionalIntegralDerivative. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: A controller can request more output than an actuator can supply. Clipping the command at the physical limits changes the behavior of the feedback loop.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: John D. Hedengren, APMonitor Process Dynamics and Control, PID lesson; https://apmonitor.com/pdc/index.php/Main/ProportionalIntegralDerivative. Consulted 2026-10-13.
